coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist, so none of the genuinely risky logic (filtering, pagination, URL state, cache) is covered by anything the team owns; the provided acceptance suite is external and won't survive a data-layer refactor.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/model.ts:1 — 400+ lines of pure, dependency-light view-model builders that would be trivial to test behaviourally and are tested not at all
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-21 — humanize/dexNumber/display are pure functions, the cheapest possible behavioural tests, still untested
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests, behavioural or otherwise.

evidence: app/src/routes/index.tsx:63-94 — debounce timer plus manual pushedQuery tracking plus createEffect(on(...)) sync: a fragile state machine with no guard against URL/signal desync on back-navigation or rapid typing

app/src/lib/server/model.ts:186-236 — move-table build: dedup key, methodRank ordering, default game = last-highest-order assumption, level/name sort — a refactor here would fail nothing owned by the app
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:60-75 — cache stores promises and evicts on rejection; a subtle bug (caching a rejected promise, limiter leak) would pass the acceptance suite silently
regression_power.rationale: With zero app-owned tests, breaking any behaviour only fails if the external acceptance suite happens to hit it; the fragile parts (debounce/URL sync, cache, sort comparators) are exactly the parts it hits shallowly.

evidence: app/package.json:6-9 — no test infrastructure, hence no noise
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests, per the rubric this scores 3; the flip side is there is also no signal at all.

findings.issue: The app ships with no test framework, no test script and zero test files; all quality gates are the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (or @solidjs/start's recommended setup) plus a `test` script, and start with unit tests for app/src/lib/server/model.ts and app/src/lib/format.ts, which are pure and need no browser.

findings.issue: homeData concentrates the app's riskiest logic — search substring match, type-in-either-slot, generation membership, 48-per-page slicing and page clamping — with no coverage; an off-by-one in the slice or a filter that stops resetting page would only be caught by the borrowed acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test homeData with a small fixture payload: filter combinations, empty results, page beyond total, and the count vs. sliced-cards relationship.

findings.issue: The search input's URL sync is a hand-rolled state machine (debounce timer, pushedQuery mirror, createEffect(on(...))) with no regression net; back/forward navigation racing a pending debounce could desync the input and the URL.
findings.suggestion: Add component tests (solid-testing-library) covering: typing updates the URL after debounce, navigating back updates the input, and typing then changing a filter resets page — or simplify the mechanism so it needs fewer tests.

findings.issue: cardsFor maps Pokémon references to species cards (alternate-form exclusion, ID dedup, species-name fallback at line 80) and is reused by move, ability and type pages; a regression here breaks four pages at once and nothing in-app would notice.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests over a fixture containing an alternate form (id > 10000), a duplicate, and a Pokémon missing from the species list.

findings.issue: The client-side sort comparator handles missing-values-last in both directions, numeric vs string columns, and a label tie-break; only the happy ascending path is exercised by the acceptance suite, so descending-with-missing-values and tie-break regressions would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the rows memo's comparator logic (extract it if needed) with null power/accuracy rows in both directions.

findings.issue: The request cache and MAX_CONCURRENT limiter are the kind of code that fails under load, not under happy-path tests: promise dedup, rejection eviction, and the waiting-shift() release path are all untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with a mocked fetch: dedup under concurrency, 404 not cached, non-404 evicted, and limiter never deadlocks when a request rejects.

findings.issue: Move-table construction assumes version-group `order` is monotonic (default = games[games.length-1] at line 200), dedups via a composite key, and orders methods via methodRank; none of these invariants are asserted anywhere owned by the app.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test pokemonMovesData with fixtures where order is non-contiguous, a move appears via two methods, and a bogus ?game= falls back to the latest.

findings.issue: A non-404 API error propagates as a thrown Error and there is no ErrorBoundary or catchError anywhere in app/src, so an API hiccup renders a raw error page with no shared layout — an untested, user-facing failure path.
findings.suggestion: Add an error boundary (or NotFound-style fallback route) and a test asserting the layout survives an API 500.

findings.issue: shortEffect's $effect_chance substitution and the latest-English-flavor-text fallback (model.ts:36-40) implement spec wording rules with no coverage; a change to entry selection order would pass unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Cheap unit tests with two English entries and an entry missing effect_entries.

findings.issue: humanize, dexNumber and display encode spec-level display rules (Mr Mime, #0025, em dash) but are untested even though they are pure one-liners.
findings.suggestion: A handful of assertions here is the highest value-per-line test in the codebase.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own: no runner, no test script, no test files. The riskiest code — home filtering/pagination, the debounce/URL-sync state machine, move-table sorting, species-card mapping and the HTTP cache — is guarded only by the externally provided acceptance suite, which tests shallow happy paths and won't protect a future data-layer refactor. Adding vitest unit tests for app/src/lib/server/model.ts and app/src/lib/format.ts would be cheap and high-value.
